note: S120h — predict-only, the remaining seventeen. Spans G1 to G12, so the register shifts with the band: the K-2 predictions are one short question about where a hand points or how many parts to cut, and the HS ones carry the misconception in the option text. Widgets asserted byte-identical by the converter.

predict.prompt: A square rug covers 36 square feet. Its side length is…
predict.reveal: 6 feet, because 6 × 6 = 36. Halving gives 18, which would be right if area were side + side — but area is side TIMES side, so undoing it takes a square root rather than a halving.

predict.prompt: A histogram's bars touch, with no gaps between them. That is because…

options.label: The bins sit next to each other on a number line, with nothing in between
The bars are always the same height
It simply looks tidier that way

predict.reveal: The bins run along a number line, and there is no space between "10–19" and "20–29" — a reading of 19.5 has to land somewhere. Bar charts separate their bars because their categories genuinely are separate things; a histogram cannot, because its categories are stretches of one continuous scale.

predict.prompt: One 1, three 2s, five 3s, three 4s, one 5. Once these are plotted, the shape will be…

options.label: Symmetric, piled up in the middle
Clustered at the low end with a long tail
Spread evenly across all five values

predict.reveal: Symmetric — counts of 1, 3, 5, 3, 1, peaking at 3 and falling away evenly on both sides. Shape is the fastest thing a plot gives you: the balance point is visible here before a single mean is calculated.

predict.prompt: For 3:15 the minute hand points at the number 3. How many minutes is that?
predict.reveal: 15 minutes. Every number on the face is worth 5 minutes to the minute hand, so the 3 means three fives. The very same number means 3 o'clock to the hour hand — one face, two different ways of counting it.

predict.prompt: One quarter and one dime together are worth…
predict.reveal: 35¢ — a quarter is 25¢ and a dime is 10¢. Counting the coins gives 2, but coins are not worth the same as each other, so how many you hold tells you nothing about how much you have. You have to add the values.

predict.prompt: For 3 o'clock, where does the LONG hand point?
predict.reveal: Straight up to the 12. The long hand at the 12 always means o'clock, whatever the hour is. It is the short hand that moves round to the 3.

predict.prompt: For half past 7, where does the LONG hand point?
predict.reveal: Straight down to the 6 — halfway round the clock, which is what half past means. The short hand sits between the 7 and the 8, because half of that hour has already gone.

predict.prompt: Which hand do you check FIRST to know whether it is o'clock or half past?
predict.reveal: The long hand. Straight up at the 12 means o'clock; straight down at the 6 means half past. Check that first, then read which hour it is from the short hand.

predict.prompt: To make thirds, how many equal parts do you cut the bar into?
predict.reveal: 3 equal parts, and one of them is a third. A half comes from 2 parts and a fourth from 4 — the name always tells you how many to cut. The parts have to be the same size, or none of them is a third.

predict.prompt: The line through (1, 1) with slope 2. Its y-intercept will be…
predict.reveal: −1. Point-slope writes it as y − 1 = 2(x − 1), and multiplying out gives y = 2x − 1. The point you were handed is not the intercept: stepping back one unit in x drops you by 2, from 1 down to −1.

predict.prompt: On y = 2x + 1, take any point and step one to the right. The next point is…
predict.reveal: 2 higher — that is precisely what slope 2 means, and the three points say it out loud: 3, 5, 7. The +1 decides where the line starts; the 2 decides how it steps, and it takes the same step every single time.

predict.prompt: The endpoints sit at 3 and 11. The midpoint is at…
predict.reveal: 7 — the average, (3 + 11) ÷ 2. The 8 is the segment's LENGTH, 11 − 3, which is a distance rather than a place. A midpoint is a coordinate, and it has to sit between the two endpoints it splits.

predict.prompt: A vertical line of symmetry means a fold down the middle matches the left half to the right. Which of these letters has one?
predict.reveal: A. Fold it down the middle and the two halves land exactly on each other. L and R have no fold that works anywhere — a shape either has a mirror that maps it onto itself or it does not, and "nearly" is not a kind of symmetry.

40 minutes: 10 to reach 2:00, then 30 more. Subtracting the minute labels gives 30 − 50 = −20, which is nonsense — the hour rolls over at 60, not at 100. Hopping to the whole hour first keeps you clear of that trap entirely.

predict.prompt: Of the 12 sectors, how many are a multiple of 3 OR a multiple of 4?
predict.reveal: 6, not 7. There are four multiples of 3 and three multiples of 4 — but 12 is on both lists and is only one sector. Adding the counts overcounts every shared outcome exactly once, which is the whole reason the addition rule subtracts the overlap.

predict.prompt: On the table, "takes the bus OR plays a sport" means shading…

options.label: The whole bus row and the whole sport column
Only the cell where the row and the column cross

predict.reveal: The whole row and the whole column. The crossing cell is the students who do both — it belongs to "or" and gets shaded, but only once. Shading only the crossing is "and", which is a different and much smaller group of students.

predict.prompt: 4 shirts and 3 hats. How many different outfits are there?
predict.reveal: 12 — each of the 4 shirts pairs with each of the 3 hats, so the branches multiply. Adding gives 7, which counts the garments rather than the outfits: you are filling one slot AND another, not choosing a single item overall.
